solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Monkey evokes catcall during prohibition

indicators.note: during means the catcall sits in the middle of the prohibition

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
boo is a jeering catcall

explanation.surface: A monkey provokes jeers while some ban is in force.
explanation.definitionFit: The baboon is a large ground-dwelling African primate, a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Spar at front end of ship piercing two ribs (broken)

indicators.note: piercing means the single letter goes through the middle of the scrambled group
broken tells us the two words are smashed and reassembled
end of means only the final letter of the word ship is used

explanation.surface: A spar at a vessel's tip has gone through a couple of ribs, which snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: '(broken)' signals the scramble, giving BOWSRIT; 'end of' picks P and 'piercing' sets it inside. The definition is 'Spar at front', not 'front end of ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is the spar that projects forward from the bow of a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Money for first bill raised by vegetable

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means this piece is read upwards

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Cash put up for an initial invoice from a greengrocer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AC (account, a bill) into CA, written upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the cabbage genus, covering vegetables like broccoli and sprouts.

clue.text: Start actors mining

parts.note: to open is to start
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Actors begin digging for minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Opencast describes mining done from an open pit at the surface rather than tunnels.

clue.text: Jersey, say, in its offspring in charge of making chalk

indicators.note: in means the islands' letters go inside the young animal

parts.note: the offspring of a Jersey cow is a calf
Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

explanation.surface: A Jersey cow's calf put in charge of chalk production.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey does double duty in the surface: a breed of cow, whose young is the calf, and an island; the wordplay uses it as CI, the Channel Islands, while 'its' points to the cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcific means forming or producing calcium carbonate, the stuff chalk is made of.

clue.text: Order matters with India's cooperation

indicators.note: cooperation suggests the letters working together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: Things go smoothly with help from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooperation' signals the rearrangement of MATTERS plus INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to manage or direct, putting things in order.

clue.text: See 3
Religious house or fish and chip shop?

definitions.meaning: a home for an order of friars
a whimsical reading as a place full of fryers, where frying happens

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: a fish and chip shop is full of fryers.
explanation.definitionFit: A friary is a monastery housing friars; the joke treats it as a place of frying.

clue.text: Tinned copy of snack

parts.note: to can food is to tin it
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: A tinned imitation of a party nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served with drinks, a snack.

clue.text: Predator one has words with

definitions.meaning: a small carnivorous mammal that hunts
... words are evasive phrasing, so this animal is something one has words with

explanation.walkthrough: Weasel words are deliberately misleading or evasive language.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a small hunting mammal, and it pairs with words to make the idiom for evasion.

clue.text: Deficiency in task initiated by love

indicators.note: initiated by means the second item is preceded by the first

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
a mission is a task

explanation.surface: Something missing from a job started for love.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a thing left out, a gap or shortfall.

clue.text: Almost catch born speaker who takes part in jobshare?

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to collar is to catch someone
an orator is a speaker

explanation.surface: Nearly nab a natural public speaker who shares a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts COLLAR to COLLA. The definition is cryptic: people sharing a job labour together.
explanation.definitionFit: A collaborator works jointly with others, as a job-sharer does.

clue.text: Not French sovereign, English one, in feast

parts.note: pas is French for not
sov is informal for a sovereign coin
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is an English sovereign

explanation.surface: Not a French monarch, just an English one, at the banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English one' means an English sovereign: ER, Elizabeth Regina. SOV is short for the sovereign coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Passover is the Jewish festival commemorating the Exodus, celebrated with the Seder feast.

clue.text: Stumble after a few drinks, ending where you started

indicators.note: after means the stumble is placed following the drinks

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: Tripping after a few pints, and finishing up back where you began.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey out and back to the original starting point.

clue.text: See 13
Move furtively, as reptile swallowing its tail?

indicators.note: swallowing its tail means the final letter is pulled back inside the word

parts.note: a snake is a reptile

explanation.surface: A serpent creeps along, like one of those mythical ones eating its own tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing its tail' moves the last letter E of SNAKE inside, between N and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneak is to move quietly and stealthily to avoid notice.

clue.text: Shock treatment binds shrinking violet to remove from home

indicators.note: binds means the treatment wraps round the shortened flower

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, shock treatment

indicators.note: shrinking means the word violet is cut down to its first two letters

explanation.surface: Electric therapy clamps down on a shy person to get them out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrinking violet' looks like a set phrase for a shy person, but it is split: 'shrinking' trims the flower and 'binds' sets the stub inside the therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from their home by legal process.

clue.text: Talk of ink on key to riddle we hear: not settled

indicators.note: talk of means the words are spoken rather than written
we hear confirms the pieces are taken by sound

parts.note: ink on, plus clue (the key to a riddle), plus sieve (a riddle is a coarse sieve)

explanation.surface: Discussing ink on the answer to a puzzle, the matter remains open.
explanation.walkthrough: Riddle has its rarer sense of a coarse sieve; key to a riddle is its clue. Said aloud, INK ON CLUE SIEVE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconclusive means not leading to a firm result or decision, unresolved.

clue.text: I get people together with some worship

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with

indicators.note: some means only part of the synonym is used

parts.note: veneration is worship

explanation.surface: A churchgoer claims to gather a congregation for prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims VENERATION to VENER.
explanation.definitionFit: A convener is the person who calls a meeting and brings people together.

clue.text: Greens at variance may break up

indicators.note: at variance suggests the letters are out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Environmental politicians who disagree may split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variance' signals the rearrangement of GREENS AT. The Greens are a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate people from one another, causing a split.

clue.text: Hide religious symbol after prohibition with equestrienne in view

indicators.note: after means the burial and symbol follow the prohibition

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
to bury is to hide
the cross is the Christian symbol

explanation.surface: Concealing a crucifix following a ban, with a horsewoman watching.
explanation.walkthrough: BANBURY CROSS is the Oxfordshire landmark of the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock horse to Banbury Cross, to see a fine lady upon a white horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the rider goes to this market cross to see a fine lady on horseback.

clue.text: Herbs for lots and lots of bees?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, lots
hives hold large colonies of bees

explanation.surface: Garden plants that attract swarms of bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are a common culinary herb of the onion family.

clue.text: Fugitive from alien regime

indicators.note: alien means strange, so the letters take a foreign shape

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing from a foreign government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' signals the rearrangement of REGIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is someone who has left their country, often fleeing political conditions.

clue.text: Call police to get compassion when given unwelcome fact

parts.note: ho is a call to attract attention
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
ruth is an old word for pity or compassion

explanation.surface: Ringing the police for sympathy after hearing bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MET is London's Metropolitan Police force; RUTH survives in 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unpleasant fact about oneself that someone points out.

clue.text: See 23
See 12
Smiles made feminine man enter market with page

indicators.note: enter means the woman-and-man pair go inside the trading word

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them
he is a male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: Grins come about when a womanly fellow joins a market with a pageboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smiles' is not grins but Samuel Smiles, the Victorian author whose 1859 book bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Smiles wrote the famous Victorian book of this name on self-improvement.

clue.text: See 26
Invite confused gentleman to produce a little sketch

indicators.note: confused means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the printed word supplies only its last four letters to the mix
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Ask a bewildered man to dash off a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, INVITE and GENT have two letters too many (I and N); the answer uses VITE with GENT, rearranged by 'confused'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a small decorative illustration or brief descriptive sketch.

clue.text: John to sign name without names

indicators.note: without means outside, so the sign-and-name pair wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
NN abbreviates names, the plural doubling the letter

explanation.surface: A man called John adds his signature without writing his names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: LEON surrounds NN.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon was the Beatles songwriter, so John identifies him by first name.

clue.text: Pas to passage with wives in film

parts.note: pas is a step in ballet
a ford is a shallow place for crossing a river

explanation.surface: A dance step leads to a corridor where wives appear on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stepford Wives (1975) is a film about suburban wives replaced by docile robots.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title The Stepford Wives completes the phrase, so wives in a film defines it.

clue.text: Passer possibly few and far between

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters could be made

explanation.surface: A passer-by, perhaps, is a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the rearrangement of PASSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, so its items are few and far between.
